whatWeDo.heading: Draft & Logic builds the systems behind your site.
whatWeDo.text: Anyone can put up a website. The hard part is what happens after someone lands: finding the right session on the first try, getting a sponsor’s form into your CRM before they close the tab, knowing which searches came up empty last week. That takes engineering, clean data and someone who actually reads the numbers.

manifesto: Search answers the easy questions now.
So the click has to count.
Not more pages. Fewer dead ends.
We build for the person who already knows what they want.

steps.text: We read your analytics and your search terms before we read the brief.

steps.title: Build

values.title: Hand over the keys.
values.text: Code, design files, domain and every account are yours from day one. Leave whenever you like.

values.title: Skip the page builder.
values.text: Hand-built pages load faster and break less. Your team still edits them in a minute.

values.title: Count what matters.
values.text: A search that found nothing tells you more than a thousand pageviews.

values.title: Say it plainly.
values.text: Written scopes, written quotes, no jargon. If something slips, you hear it from us first.

facts.q: Can you work alongside our developers or agency?
facts.a: Yes. We often build the back end, search or dashboard while another team owns the design. Every endpoint is documented, so the handoff doesn’t depend on us.
In your accounts: your analytics property, your database, your CRM. We work with delegated access, and when the project ends you remove it. Nothing sits in a studio account.

facts.q: How do you decide what to track?
facts.a: We start from the decisions you make each week, then name the events that answer them, like a registration that was started and not finished, or a search that found nothing. That list is agreed before any tracking code is written.

facts.q: Does a dashboard have to be custom?
facts.a: Not always. If Google Analytics and a Looker Studio report answer the question, we set those up and stop there. Custom is for when the numbers sit in more than one system.

facts.q: Do we have to replace our current site?
facts.a: Not always. Search, a dashboard or an integration can often be added to the site and tools you already have. The audit tells you which way costs less.

lead: We’re Draft & Logic, a Wake Forest studio for the work behind the website: search, data, dashboards and the wiring between your tools.
